title: Secure Connectivity & Evidence Manifest — RBAC v2 + mTLS + SIEM Export
content:
Purpose:
This manifest captures a recommended secure-connectivity pattern for Redwood Private deployments with explicit mappings from network controls through RBAC v2 and audit schema into downstream SIEM/evidence automation. It is intended for internal infra and security engineers responsible for onboarding new private customers or hardening existing footprints.

Scope:
- VPC design variations (peered, transit, PrivateLink) for control plane connectivity
- Minimal, auditable firewall/security group baselines for control and data paths
- mTLS and workload identity guidance (SPIFFE-compatible) for inter-service authentication
- RBAC v2 role bindings focused on network and evidence operations
- Audit log schema and recommended SIEM export/parsing for automated evidence collection
- A short hardening/runbook checklist to validate evidence readiness for audits

High-level architecture (ASCII diagram):

  [Customer VPC]                       [Redwood Control VPC]
  +----------------+                   +------------------------+
  |  Private Subnet |<--Peering/PL-->--| Control-plane Private  |
  |  - Ingress LB   |                   | - API endpoints (priv) |
  |  - svc mesh     |                   | - metrics forwarder    |
  +----------------+                   +------------------------+
          |                                      |
          | service-mesh (mTLS)                   | SIEM ingest (TLS/Proxy)
          v                                      v
  +----------------+                     +----------------+
  | Runtime nodes  |--(egress/NAT)-->---| Logging agent  |
  | (GPU pools)    |                    | (filebeat/syslog)|
  +----------------+                    +----------------+
               \                            /
                \--(S3 evidence export)----/\
                                           \/
                                      [Evidence S3 bucket]

Design patterns (short):
1) Dual-subnet separation: control-plane traffic (model control plane API, health, telemetry) must traverse a control subnet with restrictive SGs. Data-plane inference nodes live in separate service subnets.
2) Private control plane: use PrivateLink or VPC peering to avoid internet exposure for admin/control endpoints.
3) Outbound egress only via centralized NAT + proxy to enforce TLS inspection and logging.
4) Service-to-service auth: internal mTLS with SPIFFE identities issued by a central workload CA (Envoy sidecar recommended).

Baseline firewall/security group rules (apply least privilege):
- Control-subnet SG (control-sg):
  - Allow inbound TCP 443 from customer management CIDR (only PrivateLink/peered CIDR)
  - Allow inbound TCP 9411 (tracing) from observability subnet IPs
  - Deny all other inbound
- Service-subnet SG (svc-sg):
  - Allow inbound TCP 22 from jump-box SG only (for emergency maintenance, short TTL access logs)
  - Allow inbound mTLS port 15001/15002 from svc-sg (mesh sidecar)
  - Allow outbound TCP 443 to control-sg for model control calls
- Egress-proxy SG:
  - Allow outbound TLS 443 to known telemetry endpoints (SIEM, metrics)
  - Deny wide-range ephemeral outbound unless explicitly whitelisted

Note: map SGs to CIDR ranges in peerings and PrivateLink endpoints; avoid 0.0.0.0/0 except for NAT egress where necessary.

mTLS and workload identity guidance:
- Use SPIFFE/SPIRE to issue x509 SVIDs for workloads. Short TTL (1 hour) for leaf certs; CA cert rotation at least every 90 days.
- Deploy Envoy sidecars to handle mTLS termination and SNI routing. Configure TLS contexts with TLS-1.3 and AEAD ciphers.
- Mutual-auth enforcement: allow only mesh-verified identities to bind to service ports; deny direct pod-to-pod plain-TCP.
- Certificate verification logging: emit verification success/failure events to audit logs with fields (source_identity, dest_identity, cert_serial, outcome, timestamp).

RBAC v2 mapping (network & evidence roles) — minimal recommended roles:
- network-admin: manage VPCs, subnets, route tables, and SGs. Privilege: create/update/delete network resources. Audit scope: full.
- infra-operator: deploy/scale runtime nodes, restart services. Privilege: orchestration APIs for deployments. Audit scope: node lifecycle events.
- svc-identity: service principal for runtime components to call control plane. Privilege: token mint for service-to-service calls. Audit scope: token mint/usage.
- evidence-auditor: read-only access to evidence buckets, SIEM query console, and audit logs. No write privileges.
- incident-first-responder: ephemeral RBAC binding via just-in-time (JIT) mechanism for account breakout. Must require approval and be time-limited.

RBAC binding examples (conceptual):
- Bind network-admin to group: cloud-network-eng@redwood.com
- svc-identity: Kubernetes serviceAccount annotated with spiffe id and pinned to minimal IAM role via IRSA

Audit log schema (canonical fields — JSON object per event):
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- event_id: UUIDv4
- source: string (component e.g. "envoy-sidecar", "sg-controller", "auth-service")
- event_type: string (e.g. "cert_verification", "sg_change", "route_update", "token_mint", "api_request")
- actor: string (user email or service principal)
- actor_ip: string (IP or CIDR)
- resource: string (ARN/URN of resource changed/queried)
- action: string (create/read/update/delete/allow/deny)
- outcome: string (success|failure|warning)
- details: string (free-form error or context)
- trace_id: string (optional, links to distributed trace)

Retention / integrity:
- Write logs to an append-only store (S3 with object lock + kms encryption) and replicate to SIEM for analysis. Keep immutable copies for legal retention windows.

SIEM export & parsing recommendations:
- Preferred flow: local logging agent (filebeat/fluentd) -> central log-aggregator -> SIEM ingest endpoint (TLS + client cert)
- Event normalization: translate varying source names into canonical fields (source,event_type,event_id,actor,resource,outcome) at ingestion.
- Splunk/Elastic mapping hints:
  - Splunk: index = redwood_private_audit, sourcetype = redwood:audit:v1, timestamp from timestamp field, event_id as transaction id
  - Elastic: index alias = redwood-audit-YYYY.MM.DD, ingest pipeline to add ecs_compatibility and map actor to user.name, resource to url.path
- Alerting: create SIEM rules for:
  - unauthorized sg changes (event_type == "sg_change" && outcome == "success" && actor not in allowed groups)
  - cert verification failures (> 5 in 10m)
  - evidence pipeline delivery failures (s3_put_failed)

Evidence automation pipeline (automated assembly of audit artifacts):
1) Capture sources: control-plane API logs, envoy mTLS verification events, SG/route controller events, node lifecycle events.
2) Forward raw JSON events to central log-aggregator (TLS encrypted). Tag events with customer_id and deployment_id.
3) Periodic batch worker (Lambda/K8s CronJob) runs evidence-assembler that:
   - Queries SIEM for rule results and relevant events (time-bounded)
   - Pulls matching raw logs from S3 prefix (partitioned by date/customer)
   - Assembles a signed manifest.json listing artifacts and SHA256 checksums
   - Uploads manifest and artifacts to an evidence-bucket with object-lock and writes a metadata entry to a protected ledger (DynamoDB/CloudTrail combined)
4) Trigger: evidence snapshot runs after any change to network config or on weekly cadence for continuous compliance.
5) Access: evidence-auditor role can retrieve manifests; all retrievals are logged and must be recorded in the audit ledger.

Minimal automation snippets (pseudo):
- Evidence manifest entry example: {"manifest_id":"<uuid>","snapshot_ts":"2024-12-11T10:05:00Z","artifacts":["sg-change-<id>.json","envoy-verify-20241211.ndjson"],"signer":"infra-operator@redwood.com","signature":"<sig>"}

Hardening and readiness checklist (pre-audit):
- [ ] PrivateLink/peering endpoints configured with restricted principal policies
- [ ] Control-subnet SGs locked to management CIDRs only
- [ ] mTLS enforced between all runtime services; verification logs produced
- [ ] RBAC v2 bindings applied and reviewed; no long-lived elevated bindings
- [ ] Evidence S3 bucket has object lock & encryption & narrow IAM policy
- [ ] SIEM ingestion pipeline validated end-to-end (agent -> SIEM -> query)
- [ ] Weekly automated evidence snapshot runs for each customer deployment
- [ ] Alerting rules for critical network changes are enabled in SIEM
- [ ] Incident JIT RBAC flow tested and audit logged

Runbook excerpt — suspected unauthorized SG change:
1) Receive SIEM alert: "unauthorized sg_change" with event_id X
2) Pull manifest for timeframe from evidence-bucket and correlate with SIEM events
3) Identify actor field; if actor is service principal, map to pod/service account
4) If user account, trigger account hold: disable privileges and start forensic snapshot (preserve memory-sensitive artifacts per legal guidance)
5) Remediate: roll back SG change using versioned IaC template; apply temporary deny rule to control subnet if lateral risk exists
6) Document action into incident ticket; attach evidence manifest and signed checksums.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Add exact retention window for evidence bucket (legal already requires 7 years for certain customers — need policy integration)
- Harden object-lock configuration to prevent accidental deletion by infra-operators
- Evaluate using KSI/timestamping for manifest signatures for non-repudiation

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a practical starting manifest: it focuses on observable events and deterministic artifact assembly to make private deployments auditable without exposing control plane public endpoints. Feedback requested on: retention policy, masking PII in collected logs, and automating the JIT RBAC approval flow.
